newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open up 0.30 to 0.60 cent.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open up 0.30 to 0.60 cent.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open up 0.30 to 0.60 cent Wednesday as LME edged higher overnight on the back of a widening cash to three months spread.
LME stocks fell 1,125 tonnes Wednesday to 139,975 tonnes.
COMEX stocks Tuesday fell 55 short tons to 39,551 short tons.
On ACCESS, COMEX July copper traded 118.40 to 117.80 cents a lb compared with Tuesday's close of 117.85 cents.
COMEX copper closed at a one-year high Tuesday as continued labor unrest in South America, dwindling LME stocks and good demand underpinned the market.
The LME backwardation was $78/$82, slightly higher than Tuesday.

Late Tuesday a United Steelworkers of America official said labor talks at BHP Copper's operations in the U.S. had failed to reach agreement over pay and benefits, and arbitration appeared inevitable.
Under the framework agreement, the arbitrator's decision would be binding for a year. The union would not have the right to strike or be locked out by the company, the official said.
No meetings have been scheduled in the union's stalled talks with Phelps Dodge at the Chino mine in New Mexico, the official added.
